parts.title: Pit Row
parts.text: The regional robotics tournament had begun, and Anil felt nervous as he rolled his team's robot into the pit. It was **bulky**, a boxy tower of aluminum that looked like a rolling refrigerator. Across the aisle, a rival team polished a **sleek** machine shaped like a silver dart. "Ours may not be pretty," Savannah said, "but it is **versatile**. It can climb ramps, carry rings and flip switches." Kai crouched beside the lifting **mechanism**, a set of gears and pulleys, and listened for any strange clicking.

parts.title: The Glitch
parts.text: In the first round, the robot was supposed to be **autonomous**, driving itself with no remote control for thirty seconds. Instead it spun in circles. A **glitch** had crept into its code. Savannah traced the trouble to the **algorithm**, the step-by-step list of instructions that told the robot when to turn. Kai tested each **sensor**, the small device that detected walls, and discovered that a wire had come loose.

parts.title: Fixing It Fast
parts.text: During the break, Kai repaired the broken **circuit**, soldering the wire back so electricity could flow again. Anil decided to **tweak** the turning angle by only two degrees, a tiny change that mattered. Then Savannah began to **refine** the code, polishing every line until the robot moved smoothly. Finally, they tried to **optimize** its route, trimming it to the shortest path to the scoring zone.

parts.title: The Final Round
parts.text: When the second round began, the robot rolled out, turned exactly where it should and dropped its rings into the goal. The team did not win first place, but the judges awarded them a prize for problem solving. Fixing a machine under pressure, he realized, was harder and far more rewarding than building a perfect one.
